title: Disinformative Variables Named `l` and `O`
pattern: Declaring variables named with the lowercase letter `l` or the uppercase letter `O`.
why_bad: High visual ambiguity. The lowercase `l` is indistinguishable from the numeric literal `1` in many fonts, and the uppercase `O` is indistinguishable from `0`. It compiles perfectly but creates severe visual confusion.
detection: Variables, parameter bindings, or struct fields named exactly `l` or `O`.
source: *Clean Code*, Chapter 2 (p. 20) / *The Art of Readable Code*.
